title: Different oxygen counts
hook: Count the atoms and trace their bonds.

knows: Condensed structural formulas and covalent bonds.
doesNotKnow: The first structure has formula C₂H₄O₂; the second has C₂H₆O. Because the atom counts differ, this pair is not a pair of constitutional isomers.

misconception: Different-looking structural drawings must represent different formulas or different compounds.
objective: Compare molecular formula and connectivity when classifying two structures.

claims.text: Structure A is ethanoic acid (C₂H₄O₂); structure B is ethanol (C₂H₆O). The first structure has formula C₂H₄O₂; the second has C₂H₆O. Because the atom counts differ, this pair is not a pair of constitutional isomers.
Constitutional isomers have the same molecular formula but different atomic connectivity.
The diagrams show condensed connectivity, not stereochemistry or molecular geometry.

Recall: What relationship do ethanoic acid and ethanol have? The first structure has formula C₂H₄O₂; the second has C₂H₆O. Because the atom counts differ, this pair is not a pair of constitutional isomers.
